format:

filters:

---

Plots with dark backgrounds and plots with transparent backgrounds, in the
viewer's default 70% black backdrop. Each one is worth opening in light and dark
mode (the toggle in the navbar). [Renderings in R](s-renderings.html) draws a
plot for each mode instead.

The site draws R plots on white (`dev.args: bg: white` in `_quarto.yml`), so the
transparent plots set `bg = "transparent"` in their own cells. They use the
`ragg_png` device, since R's own png device tints light text drawn on a
transparent background.

The plots are drawn with this helper. `ink` colors the axes, labels, and title;
`paper` fills the plot background, and `NULL` leaves the device background.

```{r}
wave <- function(k = 1, ink = "black", paper = NULL, col = "#3B7DB8") {
  if (!is.null(paper)) {
    par(bg = paper)
  }
  par(fg = ink, col.axis = ink, col.lab = ink, col.main = ink)
  x <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 400)
  plot(
    x,
    sin(k * x),
    type = "n",
    main = paste("Wave", k),
    xlab = "x",
    ylab = "sin(kx)"
  )
  polygon(
    c(x, rev(x)),
    c(sin(k * x), rep(0, length(x))),
    col = adjustcolor(col, 0.35),
    border = NA
  )
  lines(x, sin(k * x), lwd = 2, col = col)
}
```

## Dark background {#c1 expect-open="panzoom"}

A plot on a near-black background with light gray ink. It opens on the default
backdrop, which is also dark.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in light blue on a near-black background"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 2: y = sin(2x); the area between the curve and the x-axis is shaded.

wave(k = 2, ink = "gray85", paper = "#1E1E1E", col = "#7FB8E6")
```

## Dark background, light backdrop {#c2 expect-open="panzoom"}

The [dark plot](#c1) with a light gray `backdrop` of its own.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   backdrop: "rgba(225, 225, 225, 0.92)"
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in light blue on a near-black background"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 2: y = sin(2x); the area between the curve and the x-axis is shaded.

wave(k = 2, ink = "gray85", paper = "#1E1E1E", col = "#7FB8E6")
```

## Transparent background, dark ink {#c3 expect-open="panzoom"}

A plot with a transparent background and black ink. The viewer shows it on the
page background, so its axes are readable in light mode and hard to see in dark
mode, on the page and in the viewer alike.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: ragg_png
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = "transparent")
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue with black axes on a transparent background"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 3: y = sin(3x); the area between the curve and the x-axis is shaded.

wave(k = 3)
```

## Transparent background, light ink {#c4 expect-open="panzoom"}

The [transparent plot](#c3) with light gray ink: the reverse, readable in dark
mode and hard to see in light mode.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: ragg_png
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = "transparent")
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A sine curve in blue with light gray axes on a transparent background
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 3: y = sin(3x); the area between the curve and the x-axis is shaded.

wave(k = 3, ink = "gray85")
```

## Gallery of light and dark plots {#c5 expect-open="panzoom" expect-steps="true"}

A plot on white, the [dark plot](#c1), and the [transparent plot](#c3) with
black ink, in a gallery.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: light-dark
#| dev: ragg_png
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = "transparent")
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "A sine curve in blue with black axes on a white background"
#|   - "A sine curve in light blue on a near-black background"
#|   - "A sine curve in blue with black axes on a transparent background"
#| fig-cap:
#|   - >-
#|     Wave 1: y = sin(x); the area between the curve and the x-axis is shaded.
#|   - >-
#|     Wave 2: y = sin(2x); the area between the curve and the x-axis is shaded.
#|   - >-
#|     Wave 3: y = sin(3x); the area between the curve and the x-axis is shaded.

wave(k = 1, paper = "white")
wave(k = 2, ink = "gray85", paper = "#1E1E1E", col = "#7FB8E6")
wave(k = 3, paper = "transparent")
```
